text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- BRAZIL'S CENTRAL BANK TO SWAP BRADIES FOR LONG DEBT

Central Bank International Affairs Director Gustavo Franco on Wednesday announced Brazil has offered to swap selected Brady Bonds for new 30-year global bonds. Brazil intends to issue at least $1.0 billion of the new paper through the swap involving "C" bonds, Discount bonds and Par bonds.
-- CENTRAL BANK HOLDS BASE RATE STEADY AT 1.58 PCT
Brazilian Central Bank decided to hold the Basic Interest Rate (TBC) steady at 1.58 percent and the Basic Assistance Rate (TBAN) at 1.78 percent for June, the same levels as May and April.
The Senate approved in a first-round vote a constitutional amendment that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, governors and mayors to stand for a second consecutive term.

Deputies Ronivon Santiago and Joao Maia, who were implicated in an alleged cash-for-votes scandal, resigned from Congress just hours before a congressional investigation was expected to recommend their impeachment.
-- POLICE SHOT TOWARD HOMELESS IN SAO PAULO
The preliminary results of investigations showed Military Police shot in the direction of homeless people who occupied a Sao Paulo housing complex where three squatters were killed Tuesday.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
